question: Locate the anchor function for the byte_payload field in the console.log object whose action is stream.push after selecting Binary format, selecting Encoded mode, entering the byte stream, and clicking Transform. The same byte_payload value is also written to the outgoing fetch request's X-Byte-Pack header. The anchor function is the first target-specific byte-array transformation value constructor on the dynamic behavior chain: after routing, gate checks, field collection, tuple construction, async relay, middleware, and state transit, its function body itself constructs the target observable bx_<hex>:<check> value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, wrapping a return value, or emitting to console or fetch. Return exactly one complete function as a single JSON object matching answer_format. Do not return generic utilities, event handlers, the full call chain, inactive transformer slots, output wrappers, the final console sink, or the fetch call site. Note: you may only inspect code under captures; the full codebase is not accessible.
anchor_definition_general: General rule for resolving ambiguity: a function is target-specific with respect to the observable described above if at least one statement in its body either constructs or binds the target value, writes the target field, or dispatches the target action, and removing that statement would break the observed target output under the prescribed interaction. A function is generic if it is a reusable utility, a control-flow dispatcher, or a preparation routine whose body would look the same regardless of which behavior it currently serves. The anchor is the unique target-specific function on the chain whose immediate caller is generic, equivalently the shallowest target-specific function on the path from the trigger to the sink. If a target-specific function C is called by a generic dispatcher B and itself calls a generic utility D, the anchor is C, not B or D. If a generic function A merely writes whatever its callee B returns into the target field, and B is dedicated to computing that value, the anchor is B. If the target-specific statement is one branch inside a larger function F that also handles unrelated cases, F remains a valid anchor candidate.
anchor_worked_example: Worked example from a different scenario: a checkout page emits body.order_sig_v2 after the user clicks Submit Order. The chain is: construct order draft, encode checkout state, collect async profile receipt, compose request envelope, run interceptor pipeline, select sealing interceptor, canonicalize payload fields, fold payload with receipt and pepper, compute digest, write body.order_sig_v2, send request. The sealing interceptor is the anchor because its immediate caller is the generic interceptor-pipeline dispatcher, and its own body is the highest point on the chain whose code explains why order_sig_v2 is produced. Functions below it are nested helpers or core utilities; dispatcher and request sender are wrappers; same-click values such as analytics_sig, coupon_digest, view_cache_key, and retry_fingerprint are off-chain decoys. Apply the same reasoning to this page and bundle.

function_name.description: The identifier on the function declaration line in the captured bundle slice. Use the name as it appears in captures, not a guessed source-level name.

file.description: Path to the JavaScript file under captures/ that contains the function. Must match visible_corpus.

slice.description: One contiguous source slice covering exactly one complete function body in the captured bundle.

start_line.description: 1-based inclusive start line of the function in file.

end_line.description: 1-based inclusive end line of the function in file.

start_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice begins.

end_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice ends, exclusive.

code.description: Exact source text of the complete function from start_offset to end_offset. Must start with function <function_name>( and end with the closing brace of that function.

public_constraints: Only code visible under captures is in scope.
Submit exactly one JSON object matching answer_format.response_schema; do not wrap it in markdown fences unless the evaluation harness explicitly requires that.
function_name and slice.code must refer to the same function declaration in the captured bundle.
slice.code must be one complete function with balanced braces, not a signature fragment, partial body, or multiple functions.
Return one top-1 function, not a list of candidate chains.
Do not return the final console sink or the fetch call site.
Do not return a generic DOM reader, formatter, router, middleware wrapper, or output wrapper when a more target-specific byte_payload value constructor is present.
Constrain the observable by both action and field.
The target value has bx_<hex>:<check> format and should not be confused with inactive transformer values, preview state, rendered list text, or non-target console/debug objects.
